items.t: BASF stock: Renewable-power shift marks busy week
sum: BASF outlined a lower-carbon production step on November 10, 2026, saying selected European polyisobutene products will run entirely on renewable electricity from January 2027. The announcement covers the eligible Oppanol B and Glissopal portfolio produced for external customers.

The company said the transition will combine renewable power already used at its Ludwigshafen and Antwerp sites with additional volumes attributed through a mass-balance chain-of-custody approach. Power from the Hollandse Kust Zuid offshore wind farm and long-term power purchase agreements will contribute to the supply mix.

BASF said product specifications and existing sales articles will remain unchanged, so customers will not need to requalify the products. The group also offers grades with a cradle-to-gate product carbon footprint of zero under its ZeroPCF range, subject to the stated mass-balance methodology and scope.

The move supports BASF's target of sourcing more than 60 percent of its electricity from renewable sources by 2030. The products serve applications including fuels and lubricants, chewing gum, window seals, stretch films, adhesives, automotive sealants, pipelines and electronics. Further portfolio news during the week included BASF's November 12 agreement to sell its global Mining Solutions business to SNF, with closing expected in 2027 subject to approvals.
European chemical shares remain sensitive to energy costs, industrial demand and portfolio decisions. Current market reports provide the broader market setting.
BASF's announcement sets out the product scope, timing and production arrangements. More news and analyses on BASF stock are available in the company topic.

BASF's Portfolio Overhaul: Mining Exit, Louisiana MDI Start-Up and a FairWild Nod — All Under a Fr
sum: BASF has packed a remarkable amount of corporate activity into a single week, and the market's response has been decidedly mixed. On Wednesday the chemicals giant officially commissioned a new MDI production facility at its Geismar integrated site in Louisiana, a roughly USD 1 billion investment that lifts the site's annual MDI capacity to around 600,000 tonnes. The same day, Jefferies cut its rating on the stock from "Hold" to "Underperform," keeping a price target of EUR 44.

Analyst Priyanka Patel pointed to eroding margins, overcapacity, higher gas prices and a demand recovery that has yet to materialize. The shares were up 0.3% today, a modest counterpoint to the broker's gloomier stance.

A day earlier, BASF signed an agreement to divest its global mining business to France's SNF. The deal covers roughly 140 employees and the Cork production site in Ireland, with completion expected in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions.

The transaction fits a broader pattern of portfolio pruning at the Ludwigshafen-based group. Alongside the divestment, BASF said it will produce suitable Oppanol B and Glissopal polyisobutene products for external European customers entirely with renewable electricity from January 2027. Product specifications and article numbers are to remain unchanged.

On the sustainability front, BASF has secured FairWild certification for Cegesoft SB 45 TR, a shea butter-based care active. According to the company, the independent certification confirms compliance with ecological and social standards as well as responsible sourcing practices, and applies specifically to that ingredient.

Speculation continues to swirl around BASF's ambitions regarding Evonik. Reuters reported that the chief executives and finance chiefs of the two companies met on 7 November, citing a BASF offer of EUR 24.00 per share that Evonik had previously rejected.

Deutsche Bank Research had already trimmed its view. On 26 October the bank lowered its BASF price target from EUR 60 to EUR 53 and downgraded the stock from "Buy" to "Hold," with analyst Virginie Boucher-Ferte citing uncertainty surrounding the prospective Evonik takeover.

BASF stock to sell Mining Solutions business to SNF
sum: BASF has agreed to sell its global Mining Solutions business to SNF, a French specialty chemicals company, in a portfolio transaction announced on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The announcement was carried by Yahoo Finance from a GlobeNewswire release.

The divestment follows a strategic review within BASF's Performance Chemicals division. Financial terms were not disclosed. The transaction is subject to approval by the relevant merger-control authorities and other customary closing conditions, with completion expected in 2027.

The agreement covers BASF's global Mining Solutions business, including its production site in Cork, Ireland, and approximately 140 employees. The portfolio includes leaching and flotation reagents as well as solvent-extraction products. BASF named Luprofroth, Lupromin, Luproset, LIX and LixTRA among the brands included in the transaction.

Anup Kothari, a member of BASF's Board of Executive Directors, said the company is continuously evaluating its portfolio to sharpen its strategic focus. He described SNF as a suitable owner for developing the portfolio and serving mining customers. SNF said the business would complement its existing product range and strengthen its capabilities in flotation and hydrometallurgy.

The buyer plans to maintain continuity of supply and service for customers after completion. For BASF, the agreement represents another step in reshaping its portfolio, although the release gives no estimate of proceeds or any expected earnings effect. Investors therefore still need further information on the financial contribution and timing of the disposal.

The transaction will not close immediately. Regulatory clearance and the remaining closing conditions must be completed before the business and employees can move to SNF. The expected 2027 completion date leaves the financial impact dependent on the final timetable and closing terms.

BASF stock last traded at 53.93 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 18:48 CET on Monday, November 9. The quote provides a dated trading reference, while the portfolio announcement adds a strategic development for investors following BASF's restructuring and capital allocation.

sum: Evonik continues to reject BASF's increased takeover offer after senior executives from both companies held preliminary talks over the weekend, according to a Reuters report published by Euronext on Monday, November 9, 2026. No further meeting is currently scheduled, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The talks involved the chief executives and chief financial officers of BASF and Evonik. They did not lead to formal takeover negotiations or change Evonik's position. Both companies declined to comment on the meeting, according to the Reuters report.

BASF's improved proposal values Evonik at 24 euros per share and 11.18 billion euros. Evonik rejected BASF's initial 22.15-euro-per-share offer in September and opposed the improved approach in October, saying it was not sufficient to begin formal discussions.

Evonik used the weekend meeting to argue that it was better positioned within its own planned corporate structure, according to the report. BASF has said it would honor existing agreements to preserve jobs made by Evonik if an acquisition takes place. BASF Chief Executive Markus Kamieth has described a deal as a strong German response to global competition.

The latest setback leaves BASF without a clear route toward formal negotiations. For investors, the central issue is whether BASF can demonstrate enough strategic and financial value to change Evonik's position, or whether Evonik's standalone strategy will prevail.

items.t: BASF's Louisiana MDI Start-Up Meets a Jefferies Downgrade
sum: Jefferies stripped BASF of its "Hold" rating on Tuesday, moving the chemicals giant to "Underperform" while keeping a 44-euro price target unchanged. Analyst Priyanka Patel sees operating earnings for 2027 landing 5 percent below consensus, pointing to firmer gas prices, a demand recovery that has yet to materialize, thinning margins and persistent overcapacity across the sector.
The market shrugged off the call. BASF shares added 0.2 percent on the day, building on a 0.1 percent gain in the prior session that left the stock at 54.54 euros.

Efforts to acquire Evonik remain stalled. Evonik turned down BASF's raised offer of 24 euros per share on Monday, according to Reuters, despite an initial round of talks between the two companies' leadership. No further meetings are scheduled, Reuters reported. The dpa-AFX news agency framed the same encounter as an informational exchange rather than formal takeover negotiations, and said Evonik was not conducting takeover talks with BASF on Monday.

On the operational front, BASF formally commissioned a new MDI facility at its Geismar complex in Louisiana. The company put the investment at roughly 1 billion US dollars, lifting annual capacity at the site to almost 600,000 tonnes.

BASF also disclosed a shift in how it supplies European polyisobutene customers: from January 2027, the production earmarked for external buyers will run entirely on electricity from renewable sources.

The Ludwigshafen group repurchased about 352,000 of its own shares between November 2 and November 6 inclusive, part of its ongoing buyback program. In Chile, ALTA Performance Materials signed a contract on Friday to take over BASF's local Palatal business.
Those moves follow a guidance upgrade roughly two weeks ago. For 2026, BASF now expects EBITDA before special items of between 7.4 billion and 7.8 billion euros.

BASF Wins Berenberg's Short-Term Nod but Faces a Harder 2027 Test
sum: BASF has given investors little to complain about in the near term. The harder question, according to Berenberg, is whether the earnings strength carries into 2027 — and that doubt sits at the heart of the broker's freshly published assessment following an investor event in New York.

Analyst Sebastian Bray came away with a robust picture of the group's short-term trading from Chief Executive Markus Kamieth. Even so, the bar for next year looks steep, particularly in upstream chemicals, where it is unclear whether the profitability lifted by the Iran war can be matched again. Berenberg keeps its "Hold" rating and a price target of 51.50 euros; at 54.51 euros, the shares are already trading above that mark, so the house view is more guarded than the market's.

The cautious stance sits alongside a decidedly upbeat forecast. On 28 October, BASF lifted its full-year target for EBITDA before special items to at least 7.4 billion euros, up from a previous floor of 6.9 billion euros — the second upgrade this year. A later revision narrowed the range to 7.4 to 7.8 billion euros, against an earlier span of 6.9 to 7.7 billion.

Third-quarter 2026 revenue rose 14% to 16.4 billion euros. Prices climbed roughly 12% over the period while volumes added 2%, a mix that puts the emphasis squarely on pricing power rather than extra tonnage. The ramp-up of the new Zhanjiang site in China contributed to the volume gain. Whether those higher prices can be pushed through again is the pivot on which the 2027 story turns.

Not every unit pulled in the same direction. Sales at Agricultural Solutions fell by a fifth in the third quarter, and the division slipped into the red. A broader-based improvement would strengthen the case for the group, provided the farm business can return to a positive contribution.

Alongside the numbers, BASF is keeping its deal pipeline active. On Monday it signed a letter of intent with Nox Bellcow Cosmetics to explore a strategic partnership focused on body-care formulations and ingredient technologies; the two sides will first assess whether cooperation in these areas makes sense.

sum: BASF's pursuit of Evonik has hit a familiar roadblock, but the chemicals giant is not standing still elsewhere. Talks between the chief executives and finance chiefs of the two companies took place on Saturday, yet no further meetings are currently scheduled, according to Reuters, which cited two people familiar with the matter.

Evonik is holding firm to its rejection of BASF's improved offer, an insider told the news agency. The bid values Evonik at €24 per share, or roughly €11.2 billion in total. Evonik had already turned down the sweetened proposal about two weeks ago, stating it would not enter negotiations.

Away from the negotiating table, BASF repurchased around 352,000 of its own shares last week as part of its buyback programme, with the purchases spanning Monday through Friday. Following that week of buying, the stock was quoted at €54.02.

On the divestment front, ALTA Performance Materials signed a contract with BASF on Friday to acquire the Palatal business in Chile. BASF framed the agreed sale as part of its push to concentrate on its chemical core operations.

BASF also signed an investment agreement on 3 November with Nanjing Jiangbei New Area to build a new production facility for electronic materials. According to the company, the site will be located in the Materials High-Tech Park.

The same day, BASF and ParagonCorp put pen to paper on a letter of intent to explore a possible collaboration in scientifically grounded cosmetic innovation. Separately, BASF and S&J International Enterprises announced today that they had signed a letter of intent to examine a strategic partnership in the sun care segment.
Roughly two weeks ago, BASF raised its adjusted EBITDA forecast for the full year 2026 to a range of €7.4 billion to €7.8 billion, up from a previous outlook of €6.9 billion to €7.7 billion.

BASF stock outlook rises as core businesses lift Q3 earnings
sum: BASF raised its 2026 earnings outlook after reporting stronger third-quarter results on October 28, 2026. In its BASF release, the chemical company said sales and EBITDA before special items increased from the prior-year quarter, while all four core businesses contributed to the adjusted earnings gain.

Third-quarter sales increased 14 percent to 16.4 billion euros from 14.3 billion euros a year earlier. BASF attributed the improvement mainly to a 12 percent contribution from higher prices and a 2 percent increase in volumes. Positive currency effects, particularly from the US dollar and Chinese renminbi, also supported sales.

EBITDA before special items rose 15 percent to 1.6 billion euros from 1.4 billion euros. The Chemicals, Nutrition and Care, Materials, and Industrial Solutions segments delivered substantial earnings increases that more than offset weaker results in Agricultural Solutions and Surface Technologies. The adjusted EBITDA margin remained at 10 percent.

The headline operating picture was less favorable after special items. EBITDA remained at 1.2 billion euros, while BASF recorded 437 million euros of special charges, mainly for restructuring at the Ludwigshafen site and a legal settlement in Care Chemicals. EBIT fell to a loss of 98 million euros from a profit of 232 million euros in the prior-year quarter. Net income declined to 155 million euros from 172 million euros, and reported earnings per share fell to 0.18 euros from 0.19 euros.

Adjusted earnings per share, which exclude special items and amortization of intangible assets, increased to 0.72 euros from 0.52 euros. Operating cash flow was 1.1 billion euros, down 275 million euros year over year as inventories absorbed 507 million euros of cash. Free cash flow nevertheless rose by 125 million euros to 523 million euros in the quarter.

BASF now expects 2026 EBITDA before special items of 7.4 billion euros to 7.8 billion euros, compared with its previous range of 6.9 billion euros to 7.7 billion euros. The company left its free cash flow forecast unchanged at 1.5 billion euros to 2.3 billion euros and retained its existing macroeconomic assumptions, citing continuing geopolitical and economic uncertainty.

sum: BASF picked up a pair of SPE Automotive Innovation honours this week for plastic components developed with carmaking partners, though the recognition did nothing to shield the chemicals group's stock from a broad market downdraft. The shares shed 2.9% on Friday as a global retreat from AI and semiconductor names rippled through German equities, with no link established between the decline and the award announcements.

The Ludwigshafen-based company, working alongside Stellantis and L&L Products, took the SPE Automotive Innovation Award in the Chassis/Hardware category for a composite tunnel reinforcement used in the 2027 model-year Jeep Grand Cherokee. A second project earned the top prize: BASF, Toyota and Vuteq claimed the SPE Automotive Innovation Grand Award for the thermoplastic truck bed of the 2026 Toyota Tacoma, an application that also won in the Body Exterior category.

A third accolade went to BASF with Ford and Supavut Thailand in the Materials category, recognising door-handle trim on the 2026 Ford Everest. Together the three projects span different partners and vehicle applications, underscoring the group's reach across automotive supply chains.

The stock weakness had little to do with any of that. According to the Tagesschau, the worldwide selloff in AI and chip stocks weighed on the German market as a whole, and BASF was among the weakest performers in European chemicals during morning trading, dpa-AFX reported. Worries about the future momentum of AI investment drove selling pressure across sectors rather than any fresh operating news from BASF itself.

On the operating front, the picture is brighter. Roughly two weeks ago the group lifted its full-year 2026 forecast, now projecting EBITDA before special items of EUR 7.4bn to EUR 7.8bn, up from a previous range of EUR 6.9bn to EUR 7.7bn.
Third-quarter figures released on 28 October showed sales climbing 14% year on year to EUR 16.4bn, while EBITDA before special items rose 15% to EUR 1.6bn.

Beyond automotive and core chemicals, BASF has been rolling out new applications. On 30 October its trinamiX subsidiary and Eurofins Agro Testing unveiled a joint approach to mobile feed analysis for EuroTier 2026, combining NIR spectroscopy with calibration models.

sum: BASF has spent the past fortnight buying back its own stock, raising its full-year earnings target and collecting automotive industry plaudits — yet the share price still slipped 2.5% as a global selloff in AI-related technology stocks pulled DAX investors toward the exits. Reuters reported that the retreat in US and Asian tech names prompted the withdrawal, with BASF named among the German benchmark index's losers.

The pullback came a day after a separate session in which the stock fell 2.9% amid a weak German market, with dpa-AFX citing concerns over possible tariff consequences of the US midterm elections, the Middle East conflict and investment in AI infrastructure. For investors, the question now is whether the operational improvement can provide enough support to offset that external pressure.

The third quarter of 2026 delivered sales of EUR 16.4 billion, up 14% on the prior-year period. EBITDA before special items rose 15% to EUR 1.6 billion. That figure is the most meaningful test of the company's trajectory, since it makes the operating earnings progress visible.

A single stronger quarter provides a starting point; a more durable positive view would require further results to confirm the same direction. Investors should therefore weight the interplay between business expansion and earnings development more heavily than individual product announcements.

Roughly a week ago BASF raised its EBITDA guidance for the full year 2026. The new range is EUR 7.4 billion to EUR 7.8 billion, up from a previous forecast of EUR 6.9 billion to EUR 7.7 billion. The upgrade reinforces expectations that the company can underpin the improvement over the coming months.

On Monday BASF reported the repurchase of 355,128 of its own shares for the period from 26 to 30 October inclusive. Since the programme began on 3 August, a total of 7,595,230 shares had been acquired up to and including 30 October.

Concrete operational steps also support the more optimistic case. BASF commissioned expanded production capacity for alkylpolyglucosides in Cincinnati, Ohio, on 27 October — an expansion that could support the business provided the additional capacity can be used economically.

BASF Draws a Line Under Evonik: Value for Shareholders or No Deal
sum: BASF will not chase Evonik at any price. That was the message chief executive Markus Kamieth delivered ahead of the latest twist in the standoff, and it is the yardstick against which every further move on the takeover front will now be measured. According to a Reuters report dated 28 October, any transaction would only be pursued if it created value for BASF's own shareholders — a test that must hold up economically as well as strategically.
The stock finished yesterday at €55.62, a gain of 2.5%, as investors weighed the prospect of a strategic add-on against the earnings power BASF already has in house.

Evonik rejected the improved offer on 30 October and declared it would not enter negotiations. At the same time, the group signalled a willingness to hold a purely informational, confidential exchange. Media reports put BASF's most recent bid at €24 per Evonik share, with a readiness to go higher having been discussed roughly two weeks earlier.

For shareholders, the arithmetic is straightforward: the more BASF's standalone business delivers, the more convincing any additional capital commitment has to be. A deal would look attractive only if its terms clear the bar Kamieth has set. If the two sides stay apart, BASF's own operating trajectory takes over as the dominant driver of valuation.

That trajectory has strengthened considerably. BASF reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of €16.4 billion, up 14% year on year. EBITDA before special items reached €1.6 billion, 15% above the third quarter of 2025.

The company raised its full-year guidance just over a week ago, and now expects EBITDA before special items of €7.4 billion to €7.8 billion for 2026, compared with a previous range of €6.9 billion to €7.7 billion. A bullish case rests on BASF hitting that outlook while keeping financial discipline on any acquisition.

Capital returns are already in motion. In its interim stock buyback report published Monday, BASF disclosed the purchase of 355,128 of its own shares between 26 and 30 October inclusive. Since the programme began on 3 August, the cumulative volume repurchased through 30 October stood at 7,595,230 shares.

BASF Managing Director shares her ambitions, values and commitment to Stockport with Marketing Stockport
sum: Earlier this year, global chemicals firm BASF plc appointed Lisa Kelly as its new Managing Director in the UK, based at its Stockport Exchange UK headquarters.
Lisa brought with her more than 35 years of industry experience and commitment across technical, commercial and leadership roles both overseas and in the UK since joining BASF in 1989.

Being unique as a women leader in what has traditionally been a male-dominated industry, Lisa has a passion for making a positive difference, championing diversity and inclusion, supporting opportunities for women in industry and encouraging young people to explore science and technology.
Marketing Stockport caught up with Lisa to hear more about her role at BASF, her values and her commitment to supporting and strengthening the Stockport community.

sum: Evonik's board rejected formal takeover negotiations with BASF on Friday, October 30, 2026, while leaving open a purely informational and confidential exchange. The decision keeps the specialty chemicals group focused on its independent strategy rather than opening a sale process.

European Coatings reported that BASF's second and improved offer was rejected after Evonik reviewed a letter dated October 22. The report said the proposal offered 24 euros per share and included commitments covering employees and locations. Evonik's board nevertheless declined to enter negotiations.

The latest development adds a political and shareholder dimension to the standoff. North Rhine-Westphalia's economy minister Mona Neubaur rejected a takeover, while the RAG Foundation holds about 43 percent of Evonik's shares, according to European Coatings.

The distinction between information-sharing and negotiations is material for shareholders. BASF can use the confidential channel to explain its rationale, but Evonik has not agreed to discuss transaction terms. That leaves the takeover prospect unresolved and keeps the standalone strategy at the centre of the investment case.

BASF Analysts Stay Bullish Even as Evonik Rebuffs Takeover Talks
sum: BASF's October analyst scorecard lands on the friendly side: twelve of 19 ratings carry a Buy call, against five Holds and two Sells. Yet the same consensus that leans positive offers little in the way of upside, with the average price target sitting at EUR 54.08.

That gap between recommendation and expectation is the story. A Friday close of EUR 53.30 already puts the stock within touching distance of the mean target, so the bullish majority on its own is no argument for a big remaining re-rating.

Individual targets published in October run from EUR 40 to EUR 61, a range that shows how far apart analysts stand on what the shares are actually worth. The average smooths those differences without resolving them, which means the headline count of Buy ratings tells only half the tale. What matters just as much is the valuation scenario sitting behind each call.

Recent revisions illustrate the point. Deutsche Bank Research cut BASF to Hold from Buy on Monday, trimming its target to EUR 53 from EUR 60, citing greater complexity, execution risk and a heavier concentration on Europe. Bernstein Research moved the other way on conviction, keeping its Outperform rating on Thursday while shaving its target to EUR 59 from EUR 61.

Behind the caution lies BASF's approach to Evonik. According to media reports, BASF is offering EUR 24 per share, valuing Evonik's equity at roughly EUR 11.2 billion — a premium of about 39% to the price before takeover interest became public.

Evonik reviewed BASF's letter and declined to enter negotiations on that basis, though it left the door open to a confidential exchange of information only. Formal talks have not begun, and Reuters reported that BASF met the refusal with incomprehension. Chief executive Markus Kamieth had stressed on Wednesday that BASF would not overpay for Evonik, saying any transaction would go ahead only if it created value for BASF shareholders.

For BASF investors, the two threads stay separate: analysts lean positive on the stock, while the fate of the takeover push remains unresolved. Nothing in the published targets amounts to a verdict on a possible deal.

The number of full-time positions at BASF's headquarters in Ludwigshafen fell below 30,000 in May for the first time since 1954.
The development comes as chief executive Markus Kamieth presented the final figures for the second quarter, confirming preliminary results published two weeks ago.

"We have reduced our costs, cut capital expenditure and increased the utilization of our plants," Kamieth said. He said BASF had cut more jobs in the first half of 2026 than in the previous two years combined.

From January 2024 to the end of June 2026, the company eliminated around 7,000 positions worldwide, he said. The figure does not include headcount reductions resulting from divestments or the expansion of staff at the integrated production site in Zhanjiang, China.
In the second quarter, net income surged to €4.14 billion ($4.72 billion) from €79 million last year. Earnings per share were €4.78, up from €0.09 a year ago.
The latest results included a gain after taxes of €3.5 billion from the sale of BASF's coatings business to Carlyle.

sum: What major events shaped the global auto industry this week?

According to Nikkei, soaring fuel prices driven by conflict in the Middle East and rising ownership costs pushed electric vehicle sales to monthly records in 37 countries during March or April. Consumers are flocking to EVs as a cheaper alternative.

As purchase subsidies phased out in multiple nations, EV sales had previously softened. But the energy crisis has reshaped consumer choices, dramatically boosting the appeal of new-energy vehicles. This marks a turning point where global EV adoption is shifting from policy-driven incentives to organic market demand.

Data from S&P Global Mobility shows that among the 150 countries tracked, 28 nations—including Australia and the UK—saw March EV sales hit all-time highs, while nine others, including Brazil and the Philippines, set records in April.
Across March and April combined, 91% of countries posted year-over-year sales growth. It’s the first time since April 2023 that the share of countries with rising EV sales has topped 90%.

In South Korea, which relies heavily on crude oil imports from the Middle East, cumulative EV sales for March and April surged 140% year-on-year to top 80,000 units. The penetration rate for new EVs jumped 14 percentage points to 26%.
Southeast Asia’s EV sales climbed 40% to 90,000 units, capturing a 16% share of the local new car market. Meanwhile, the EU shook off its previous slump, with sales rising 40%.

Tamarac Receives Over $1 Million in 'Forever Chemicals' Lawsuit Settlements; Commission to Weigh Distribution of Funds Wednesday
sum: The Tamarac city commission on Wednesday will discuss how to allocate $315,195.02 in funds the city received as its net share of a national class action settlement over contamination of public water systems with PFAS, a group of synthetic “forever chemicals.”

The agenda item, requested by Vice Mayor Marlon Bolton, is titled “Discussion and Consensus on Allocation of a Portion of the $315,195.02 Settlement Proceeds Related to the PFAS Water Quality Class Action Lawsuit to Commission Members who Elect to Opt-In for the Benefit of Tamarac Residents.” The item calls for discussion and consensus rather than a formal vote.

The $315,195.02 represents Tamarac’s net proceeds from a settlement with BASF Corporation in Tamarac, Florida vs. Tyco, et al., a class action suit, city records show. Numerous municipalities, including Tamarac, have alleged that they have suffered harm resulting from the presence of PFAS in drinking water and/or the need to monitor for the presence of PFAS in drinking water, and that Tyco is liable to them for damages and compensation.

BASF’s gross contribution to Tamarac was $338,919.38, city records show. Ferraro Law, which represented the city in the litigation, deducted seven percent in attorneys’ fees — amounting to $23,724.36 — under a retainer agreement, leaving the city with $315,195.02 from that settlement.
On April 22, City Attorney Hans Ottinot wrote to commissioners to notify them that the check had arrived.
“Please note that the City recently received a settlement check in the amount of $315,195.02 relating to the PFAS or water quality class action lawsuit,” Ottinot wrote in an email.

PFAS — polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly called “forever chemicals” — are a family of man-made chemicals that last indefinitely in the environment and the human body. They have been linked to health risks including thyroid disorders, certain cancers, and immune system effects.

items.t: Why BASF's (ETR:BAS) Earnings Are Better Than They Seem
sum: BASF SE's (ETR:BAS) recent earnings report didn't offer any surprises, with the shares unchanged over the last week. Our analysis suggests that shareholders might be missing some positive underlying factors in the earnings report.

To properly understand BASF's profit results, we need to consider the €480m expense attributed to unusual items. While deductions due to unusual items are disappointing in the first instance, there is a silver lining. When we analysed the vast majority of listed companies worldwide, we found that significant unusual items are often not repeated. And, after all, that's exactly what the accounting terminology implies. If BASF doesn't see those unusual expenses repeat, then all else being equal we'd expect its profit to increase over the coming year.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Unusual items (expenses) detracted from BASF's earnings over the last year, but we might see an improvement next year. Based on this observation, we consider it likely that BASF's statutory profit actually understates its earnings potential! Furthermore, it has done a great job growing EPS over the last year. At the end of the day, it's essential to consider more than just the factors above, if you want to understand the company properly. In light of this, if you'd like to do more analysis on the company, it's vital to be informed of the risks involved. Case in point: We've spotted 2 warning signs for BASF you should be mindful of and 1 of these doesn't sit too well with us.

This note has only looked at a single factor that sheds light on the nature of BASF's profit. But there is always more to discover if you are capable of focussing your mind on minutiae. Some people consider a high return on equity to be a good sign of a quality business. sum: For more than twenty years, the Cologne native has been intensively involved with the stock market, both professionally and privately. He is particularly passionate about national and international small and micro caps.

This interesting commodities stock is new on the German stock market: Strategic Resources. With a market capitalization of around CAD 16 million, it is currently modest. But this could change soon. The company specializes in the development of critical minerals. The focus is on high-purity iron, vanadium, and titanium. Its flagship projects are the construction-ready BlackRock project in Quebec, Canada, and the historic Mustavaara mine in Finland.

BlackRock is set to become the first VTM (vanadium, titanium, and magnetite) mine in North America. Additionally, the project is set to feature metallurgical facilities with the lowest CO₂ emissions worldwide. This is to be achieved through green hydrogen. The latest announcement is particularly exciting. Strategic Resources plans to collaborate with battery developer Tyfast Energy to drive vertical integration in the North American raw materials and energy sector. Together, they aim to establish a domestic supply chain for vanadium-based battery materials. The focus is on processing battery-grade vanadium oxide from the BlackRock project. It will then be used in Tyfast's lithium-vanadium oxide anodes for high-performance batteries. The goal of the collaboration is to secure critical raw materials in the region and reduce dependence on global supply chains.

Both companies see great potential for their products in demanding applications in mining, defence, and industrial off-road systems, where fast charging cycles, high robustness, and cold resistance are critical. Strategic Resources is contributing its Canadian vanadium assets and processing expertise, while Tyfast is handling material validation and further development of the anodes. Should the qualification process be successful, this could lead to a fully integrated "from mine to battery" approach that strengthens Canada's position as a hub for high-quality battery materials while simultaneously creating a resilient supply chain to meet the growing demand for high-performance batteries.

items.t: BASF Q1 Profit Climbs as Glasurit, R-M Sale to Carlyle Nears Close
sum: Collision repair shops that rely on BASF's Glasurit or R-M refinish brands are moving closer to an ownership change. BASF reported first-quarter 2026 net income of €927 million (approximately $1.1 billion) on April 30 — up from €808 million in the prior-year quarter — and confirmed on its earnings call for analysts and investors that the previously announced sale of its Coatings division to funds managed by The Carlyle Group, in partnership with the Qatar Investment Authority, remains on track to close in the second quarter of 2026.

CFO Dr. Dirk Elvermann presented the quarterly figures in advance of the BASF Annual Shareholders' Meeting in Mannheim on April 30. On the analyst call, Elvermann described the quarter as unfolding in two distinct phases: moderate growth in January and February, driven in part by China, followed by a sharp shift in market conditions in March after the escalation of the Middle East conflict and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz to seaborne transport of oil, gas, and chemicals.

The binding agreement between BASF, Carlyle, and QIA, announced in October 2025, values the Coatings business — which includes automotive OEM coatings, automotive refinish coatings, and surface treatment businesses — at approximately $9.0 billion (€7.7 billion). BASF will retain a 40% equity stake in the new company, with Carlyle becoming the majority owner.

Elvermann reiterated on the earnings call that BASF expects to receive pre-tax cash proceeds of approximately €5.8 billion (approximately $6.8 billion) upon closing, subject to customary regulatory approvals.

EBITDA before special items for the first quarter came in at €2,356 million (approximately $2.8 billion), down €140 million from €2,500 million in the prior-year quarter. Currency effects — primarily from the U.S. dollar and the Chinese renminbi — reduced results across all segments.

Elvermann noted on the analyst call that without those currency headwinds of more than €100 million, EBITDA before special items would have matched the prior-year level. The EBITDA margin before special items declined to 14.7% from 15.1%.
EBIT reached €1,261 million (approximately $1.5 billion), up €102 million from the prior-year quarter. Earnings per share rose to €1.06 from €0.91.

items.t: The Precedent : Federal Circuit Affirms Antitrust Liability for Patent Tying in Ingevity Corp. v. BASF Corp
sum: In this edition of The Precedent, we outline the decision in Ingevity Corp. v. BASF Corp.

In Ingevity Corp. v. BASF Corp., the Federal Circuit affirmed a jury verdict finding that Ingevity Corp. (Ingevity) violated antitrust laws by tying licenses to its fuel‑vapor canister patent to purchases of its unpatented carbon honeycombs. The Federal Circuit upheld a trebled damages award totaling more than $84 million and rejected Ingevity’s arguments that its honeycombs were not staple goods — which would have permitted Ingevity to control the honeycombs — that its conduct was immune from antitrust laws because it has the ability to enforce its patents and that the award must be vacated because BASF Corp. (BASF) failed to disaggregate damages.

- Did BASF present sufficient evidence for the jury to find that Ingevity’s carbon honeycombs were staple goods with substantial non‑infringing uses, which would defeat Ingevity’s patent misuse defense?
- Was Ingevity’s conduct immune from antitrust liability because Ingevity’s actions involved patent enforcement activity and communications about patent rights?
- Was the jury’s antitrust damages award, including its treatment of causation and apportionment, supported by the record?
- Substantial evidence supported the jury’s finding that Ingevity’s honeycombs were staple goods that could be used in non‑infringing applications, which defeated Ingevity’s patent misuse defense.
- Ingevity had waived its immunity argument by failing to raise it before the trial court. The trial court did not commit any plain error that warranted relief.

Parkinson’s risk increases with exposure to common chemical, study suggests
sum: A pesticide commonly used in America’s food supply has been linked to Parkinson’s disease, new research suggests.
A UCLA study published in the journal Springer Nature Link suggests that exposure to chlorpyrifos could increase the risk of the neurological disease.
The chemical is often used on agricultural products like soybeans, fruit and nut trees, broccoli, cauliflower and other row crops, according to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency.
The study compared 829 people with Parkinson’s to 824 people without the disease over a 45-year period, focusing on their proximity to chlorpyrifos.
The researchers also conducted mouse experiments, where mice inhaled the pesticide as humans would for 11 weeks. Experiments were also carried out on zebrafish to study cell-level brain damage.
In humans, the study revealed that long-term exposure to chlorpyrifos led to more than a 2.5 times higher risk of Parkinson’s.
In mice, exposure to the pesticide caused movement problems similar to Parkinson’s symptoms, loss of dopamine-producing neurons, increased brain inflammation and build-up of harmful proteins.

BASF Shares Creep Toward 52-Week Peak as AgChem Spin-Off and Analyst Downgrades Pull in Opposite Dir
sum: The chemicals giant finds itself at an unusual crossroads: its stock is trading within striking distance of a yearly high, yet the analyst community is growing noticeably cooler on the shares. Two separate research houses — MWB among them — trimmed their recommendations on BASF from "Buy" to "Hold" on Wednesday, citing a familiar refrain: the valuation gap to fair value has closed, and a fresh catalyst has yet to emerge. Price targets remain pinned at €55.00.

The market's response was telling. Rather than punishing the stock for the downgrades, BASF shares edged up 1.3% to €53.45, leaving the paper just 2.9% shy of its 52-week high of €55.05. That resilience speaks to the structural supports underpinning the stock — cost savings programs and an ongoing share buyback — even as the free cash flow conversion continues to draw criticism from the sell-side.

MWB framed its decision around a "normalized risk-reward profile," suggesting the asymmetry that once favored upside has flattened after months of strong price appreciation. The implication for investors is straightforward: the tailwind from obvious undervaluation has largely played out, and further gains will now require concrete operational triggers rather than a simple re-rating.

Operationally, the picture is more complicated. BASF was forced to postpone the planned commissioning of a facility at its Industriepark Lausitz site in Schwarzheide on Wednesday after an attack on a substation near Jänschwalde disrupted regional power supplies. The site, part of the group's battery materials operations, sits within the 300-hectare industrial park. No new start-up date has been announced.

The delay is an unwelcome wrinkle for a division that forms part of BASF's strategic growth ambitions in the energy transition space, though it appears to be an external disruption rather than a reflection of any internal execution issues.

Meanwhile, the planned carve-out of BASF's agricultural chemicals division is gathering pace. Board member Livio Tedeschi confirmed last Wednesday that the separation of the business in North and South America and Europe is now largely complete, with Asia expected to follow by year-end.

Boosting solar resilience through Xfloat and BASF collaboration
sum: Xfloat Ltd., a pioneer in floating solar technology, has partnered with BASF to improve the longevity and sustainability of floating photovoltaic (FPV) systems. This collaboration brings together Xfloat’s innovative sun-tracking platforms (FPV-T) and an advanced light stabilizer solution from BASF to deliver durable, high-performance solar solutions for global deployment.

Together, Xfloat and BASF have integrated Tinuvin® 2730 ED, a proprietary light stabilization solution from BASF that protects High Density Polyethylen (HDPE) from degradation, into the float design to ensure long-term durability in demanding environments. By incorporating the additive solution into its HDPE float design, Xfloat enables the floats to withstand harsh environmental conditions for over 30 years, aligning with the lifespan of solar modules. This durability reduces maintenance and replacement costs, contributing to a lower levelized cost of electricity (LCOE).

“At Xfloat, we aim to redefine what is possible in floating solar by combining intelligent design with environmental responsibility. Partnering with BASF has enabled us to enhance the durability of our systems with materials that meet the highest performance and safety standards – especially for sensitive applications like drinking water reservoirs,” said Avi Alcalay, Chief Technology Officer, at Xfloat.

The stabilizer complies with stringent drinking water regulations, including the EU Drinking Water Directive (EU) 2020/2184, Article 11(2)(b). The Xfloat systems are certified under NSF-61 section 5 and suitable for deployment in sensitive environments such as drinking water reservoirs.

Xfloat’s technology is already being deployed in the United States, the Middle East, Europe, and Southeast Asia. A recent project in Singapore demonstrated a 28 percent yield improvement using their proprietary FPV-T. With a growing global pipeline, Xfloat is scaling its operations to meet increasing demand for resilient and efficient solar energy solutions.

BASF Launches WALLTITE® RSB Sustainable Closed-Cell Spray Foam
sum: WYANDOTTE, MI – December 15, 2025 – BASF is expanding its spray polyurethane foam (SPF) portfolio with WALLTITE® RSB, a next-generation, closed-cell spray polyurethane foam. In response to the growing demand for more sustainable building materials, WALLTITE RSB combines industry-leading performance with a blend of recycled and renewable content for a lower overall carbon footprint.

BASF engineered the system with a proprietary resin formulation that incorporates both recycled and biobased raw materials. The result is a spray foam insulation solution that enables customers’ green transformation with transparent, third-party verified environmental benefits, including reduced embodied carbon.

“We want to create double-added value for our customers by providing high-performance and sustainable solutions, “said Nancy Houle, BASF Business Director for Spray Polyurethanes North America, “WALLTITE RSB supports green building programs by offering two key advantages: it can improve the energy efficiency throughout the building’s lifespan and lower embodied carbon from the outset of construction.”

WALLTITE RSB’s credentials include pending USDA BioPreferred® Program certification and UL Solutions validation of recycled and biobased content. In addition, a manufacturer-specific Environmental Product Declaration (EPD) confirms measurable reductions in embodied carbon compared to conventional formulations.[3] These accreditations make WALLTITE RSB an ideal option for projects pursuing LEED® certification, meeting EPA Preferred Purchasing recommendations, or aligning with both public and private sector low-carbon construction mandates.

items.t: APB Resources files arbitration claim against BASF PETRONAS Chemicals over alleged unpaid amounts
sum: KUALA LUMPUR (Dec 4): APB Resources Bhd (KL:APB) said its wholly owned subsidiary has filed a claim with an arbitral tribunal against BASF PETRONAS Chemicals Sdn Bhd for alleged unpaid contract sums and payment for additional works.

In a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Thursday, APB said Amalgamated Metal Corporation (M) Sdn Bhd (AMC) is seeking payment for a remaining sum of €1.85 million (RM8.82 million) under a 2017 contract, as well as €439,482 (RM2.10 million) for additional works carried out for a steam boiler and turbine package project.

Under the contract, AMC was the on-shore consortium partner while Christof Projects GmbH was the off-shore consortium partner appointed by BASF PETRONAS Chemicals, a Malaysia-based joint venture between BASF and Petroliam Nasional Bhd (PETRONAS), for supply, installation, and commissioning works.

According to APB, AMC had completed its scope of works for the project in May 2019 and invoiced BASF PETRONAS Chemicals in accordance with the agreed payment procedures, but the company “failed, neglected and/or refused” to make the remaining payments.

The filing of the statement of claim follows a notice of arbitration by AMC and an unsuccessful jurisdictional challenge by BASF PETRONAS Chemicals before the tribunal. Following the dismissal, BASF PETRONAS Chemicals subsequently sought to set aside the tribunal's decision through an application at the High Court of Singapore.

"In accordance with the directions given by the tribunal, AMC has now served the statement of claim on BASF PETRONAS Chemicals to formally commence the substantive arbitral process while awaiting the outcome of Singapore High Court proceedings," APB said. "AMC will continue to pursue its rights and remedies under the contract."

APB said the financial impact of the arbitration is subject to the final outcome of the proceedings, noting that the amount claimed had been fully impaired in the previous financial year and may be reversed in the event of a successful recovery.
